experiments.title: Diagnostic completion
experiments.hypothesis: Two legal-observation native OpenBW clients can complete a headless game and emit replay files.
experiments.conclusion: Supported for WorkerRush versus Idle; competitive strength and long-match synchronization remain unverified.

experiments.title: Competitive bot ports
experiments.hypothesis: McRave and ZZZKBot can run natively without disabling gameplay.
experiments.notes: Both native ports completed real headless games and passed official BWAPI header compilation. The cohort remains uncalibrated and source revisions are not ladder binary matches.
experiments.conclusion: McRave and ZZZKBot are runnable native ports with archived replays; broader reliability and strength calibration remain separate.

experiments.title: Scenario control and repeatability
experiments.hypothesis: Matched map, seed, revision, and launch settings will make repeated games suitable for calibration.
experiments.notes: Fixture runs exercised the 424242 scenario-control path; these are calibration infrastructure checks, not strength evidence.
experiments.conclusion: Three controlled fixture runs completed or recorded with stable scenario inputs; calibration still requires representative bot games.

experiments.title: UAlbertaBot cross-race port
experiments.hypothesis: The MIT UAlbertaBot port can complete a native OpenBW cross-race game with normal gameplay systems enabled.
experiments.notes: Protoss UAlbertaBot versus Zerg ZZZKBot completed on Benzene; this is compatibility evidence, not historical ladder strength evidence.
experiments.conclusion: Completed with verified opposing results, LF3, zero exits, and archived replays.

experiments.title: McRave defeat shutdown repair
experiments.hypothesis: The McRave lifecycle repair will eliminate the post-defeat Destination crash without changing strategic behavior.
experiments.notes: AddressSanitizer verification was clean, but its result metadata had an opposing-winner failure caveat; release verification later completed with opposing results, LF3, empty stderr, and two hashed replays.
experiments.conclusion: Lifecycle reliability evidence improved; the ASAN caveat means this does not establish full reliability or strategic equivalence.

experiments.title: OpenBW shutdown and timer lifetime repairs
experiments.hypothesis: Correcting queued-handler and timer state lifetimes will eliminate the reproduced engine memory errors without changing bot policies.
experiments.notes: Exact Destination seed-1002 release reproduction and full default AddressSanitizer check completed. Earlier partial shared-state builds were superseded after review caught two pointer-value predicates; they remain archived.
experiments.conclusion: Verified opposing terminal results, zero exits, empty stderr and two replays in both corrected checks. This establishes the tested lifetime paths, not broad synchronization correctness.

experiments.title: Profile the slow McRave cross-race game
experiments.hypothesis: McRave policy work dominates the slow Destination game; a source subsystem will account for at least 20% of sampled runtime.
experiments.notes: Ten seconds of sampling yielded 7,780 main-thread samples. Both clients completed the profiled game; instrumentation and different openings limit performance comparison.
experiments.conclusion: Goal assignment accounted for 47.6% of samples, with repeated ground-distance calculations at 45.8%. Repeated nearest-unit scans recompute paths for a growing army. No policy change was made in this experiment.

experiments.title: Cache distances within goal assignment
experiments.hypothesis: Reusing ground distances within one assignment call will reduce repeated path searches while preserving selection order.
experiments.notes: Official-header compilation and an ordered model check passed. Candidate and baseline selected different randomized openings; comparison engines also differed. No complete candidate replay was emitted before the wall cap.
experiments.conclusion: Candidate reached 231.8 frames/s versus 189.9 in a prior unsampled run, but both timed out and trajectories differed. This is preliminary performance evidence; no causal speedup, strength gain or baseline adoption is established. A controlled bot-seed comparison is next.

experiments.title: Compare goal caching with seeded openings
experiments.hypothesis: With matching engine and bot seeds, the distance cache improves throughput while preserving compatible early commands.
experiments.notes: Four games completed cleanly, and the openings matched within both pairs. The command-compatibility gate failed at frame 3: worker order and tied mineral targets differed. Source inspection traced this to containers ordered by object pointers.
experiments.conclusion: Candidate throughput was 7.78% and 10.99% higher, but differing trajectories prevent a causal performance claim. No strength gain or baseline promotion. A subsequent stable-traversal repeat also failed; compare both selectors on identical live states next.

experiments.title: Check whether unit-ID traversal repeats
experiments.hypothesis: Sorting workers and minerals by public unit ID will make identical seeded opening commands repeatable.
experiments.notes: Two identical baseline games completed, but raw commands differed at frame 2 and mineral targets differed at frame 3. Source inspection found that OpenBW BWAPI assigns public unit IDs in first-access order from a pointer-hashed container.
experiments.conclusion: The repeatability gate failed. No candidate game was launched and no speed or strength comparison was made. Further traversal changes were stopped as planned.

experiments.title: Correct station defense coordinates
experiments.hypothesis: One station-defense insertion stores a relative offset where consumers require an absolute map tile; correcting it will remove invalid defense candidates.
experiments.notes: The diagnostic baseline exposed out-of-map defense (0,-3) at base (64,118). The one-line candidate produced absolute tile (64,115), and all recorded defense entries were valid. Both games completed and retained both-player replays.
experiments.conclusion: The replay confirms an accepted Creep Colony build at corrected tile (64,115), frame 3,542. Accept the coordinate repair for integration; no win-rate or strength improvement is inferred from these two games.

experiments.title: Compare goal selectors on identical live states
experiments.hypothesis: The cached and original goal selectors choose identical ordered units from the same live state, while caching reduces distance queries.
experiments.notes: The corrected diagnostic completed 5,780 goal-assignment calls and 2,124 actual selections with zero differences between both shadow selectors and original gameplay. A pre-review attempt was interrupted and preserved.
experiments.conclusion: The largest call had three eligible units and requested two. The required large-state coverage was 20 eligible and 10 requested, so this does not validate the profiled hotspot or establish a speed improvement.

experiments.title: Exercise goal caching with the profiled opening
experiments.hypothesis: Reusing the opening from the profiled slow game will expose large real goal-selection calls and allow both algorithms to be compared on identical states.
experiments.notes: The targeted diagnostic compared 53,828 real calls and 352,160 actual selections with zero divergences. First qualifying state: 48 eligible units, 10 requested; largest recorded state: 154 eligible, 22 requested. It hit its 180-second instrumentation cap and emitted no final result or replay.
experiments.conclusion: The registered large-state equivalence gate passed. Cached selection made 1,243,302 distance calls versus 15,122,188 original calls (91.78% fewer). Accept this evidence for a release-build quick check; these timings and the partial game establish no production speed or strength gain.

experiments.title: McRave coordinate repair and goal-cache quick check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen coordinate-repair and invocation-cache build completes the ten-game suite cleanly and sustains at least 384 durable frames per second.
experiments.notes: Nine verified games: eight wins and one loss. All 20 replays retained. The final game had two winner=true callbacks despite zero exits, and remains unscored. Overall 403.0 fps; five games below 384, slowest 322.5. Failure subtype corrected with raw collection preserved.
experiments.conclusion: The registered reliability and per-match performance requirements failed. Resolve the outcome conflict and profile the remaining slow cases before adoption. Results are uncalibrated and do not establish a causal strength improvement.

experiments.title: Stardust native compatibility smoke
experiments.hypothesis: The pinned Stardust source can run its normal Protoss gameplay path as a native ARM64 module against this project's OpenBW ABI.
experiments.notes: Frozen package b6097c9a5d972afc4d687ed51f0d001af36f50a93dc625d66eb546bd02f6080c ran against WorkerRush Zerg on Benzene with engine seed 5201 and a 120-second limit. Both processes exited zero, results opposed, LF3 held, stderr was empty, and both replays were retained.
experiments.conclusion: Native ABI interoperability and one complete smoke game are established. This single match does not estimate strength, timing representativeness, broader matchup/map compatibility, or tournament eligibility.
experiments.limitations: Uncalibrated; one game; Stardust wall-clock and address-dependent behavior uncontrolled; derivative competition use requires written author permission.

experiments.title: Profile McRave after goal caching
experiments.hypothesis: A remaining cohesive subsystem accounts for at least 20% of main-thread samples after goal caching.
experiments.notes: One preregistered 10-second sample after frame 10,080: 7,843 main-thread samples. BWEB path generation appears in at least 22.08%; goal-distance work in 0.24%; visual work in at most 0.13%. The game completed with opposing results.
experiments.conclusion: Investigate flying-navigation path generation. This sampled interval identifies CPU work; it does not establish a speedup or playing-strength improvement.

experiments.title: Investigate conflicting engine winners
experiments.hypothesis: One attempt with the failing scenario inputs may reproduce reciprocal winner callbacks and identify the terminal event ordering.
experiments.notes: The original game has contradictory local replays with reciprocal Dropped events. The one registered reproduction completed with opposing results on a different trajectory. Source review shows several engine paths produce the same drop code.
experiments.conclusion: The cause is unresolved. Preserve the original as unscored and identify the drop source with an isolated diagnostic build before changing engine behavior.

experiments.title: Identify engine drop causes
experiments.hypothesis: Logging the first engine drop source and terminal callback ordering will distinguish routine cleanup from the historical conflicting-winner failure.
experiments.notes: One WorkerRush/Idle control and one competitive attempt both completed normally. Both showed defeat, then victory 31 frames later. Their first drop followed an action from an already-defeated player; neither logged a state-hash mismatch.
experiments.conclusion: The original failure remains unclassified. Retain diagnostic logging for subsequent experiments; no shutdown-protocol change is justified by these runs.

experiments.title: Compare A* bounds checks on identical inputs
experiments.hypothesis: Caching map dimensions within each A* search preserves reachability, distance, ordered path tiles and callback counts.
experiments.notes: One registered game compared 13,439 calls, including 8,509 valid flying searches, 4,928 valid ground searches and two invalid-endpoint probes. There were zero mismatches. Independent source review passed. No naturally failed valid search occurred.
experiments.conclusion: Build a production candidate for a separate throughput evaluation. The shadow check establishes equivalence for observed calls, not a speed or strength improvement.

experiments.title: Stardust cross-race compatibility check
experiments.hypothesis: The native Stardust port completes four cross-race games with plausible production and at least 384 durable frames per second in each game.
experiments.notes: Three wins from three clean games, all above 1,700 fps. The first game crashed in Stardust mining optimization; it remains a failure. Replay commands show Protoss worker, building and combat production in every game. No state-hash mismatch was logged.
experiments.conclusion: Repair the mining-optimizer crash before accepting Stardust as a reliable opponent. These four games do not establish local Elo or BASIL-equivalent strength.

experiments.title: McRave A* bounds throughput check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen A* dimension-snapshot candidate completes ten fixed games cleanly with at least 384 durable logical frames per wall second in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Ten wins from ten clean games, with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and 20 archived replays. Games 5–10 missed the 384 fps floor; aggregate throughput was 373.9 fps. The fixed cohort is uncalibrated and does not establish a strength improvement.
experiments.conclusion: The registered performance gate failed. Preserve this candidate as an experiment and investigate repeated pathfinding callback work before another throughput check.

experiments.title: Diagnose Stardust mining timer exhaustion
experiments.hypothesis: Excluding the only remaining timer value leaves an empty prediction set that the mining forecast cannot safely consume.
experiments.notes: One preregistered probe stopped deliberately at frame 765 after observing the set change from {0} to empty. The original crash and this diagnostic attempt remain archived.
experiments.conclusion: The empty prediction set is confirmed. Test a conservative fallback in a separate fork; this deliberate abort provides no strength result.

experiments.title: Repair Stardust mining timer exhaustion
experiments.hypothesis: Restoring the possible nonzero timer values after a contradictory prediction prevents the confirmed empty-set failure while keeping the mining optimizer active.
experiments.notes: The single registered probe completed with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and replay evidence of worker, building and combat production. Recovery occurred at least eight times; the defensive forecast fallback was not used.
experiments.conclusion: The focused repair probe passed. Evaluate the frozen fork in the four-game compatibility cohort before accepting it as an opponent.

experiments.title: Validate the repaired Stardust fork
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen mining-timer repair completes all four cross-race scenarios cleanly with plausible gameplay and at least 384 durable fps in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Four wins from four clean games. Every game exceeded 1,999 fps; aggregate throughput was 2,059.4 fps. No state-hash mismatch or defensive forecast fallback occurred. Replay commands show worker, building and combat production in every game.
experiments.conclusion: Accept this frozen fork as a provisional local opponent. The original port remains rejected; this compatibility check does not establish a local Elo or transfer the upstream BASIL rating.

experiments.title: Compare cached pathfinding queries on identical inputs
experiments.hypothesis: Caching heuristic and walkability results within one search preserves each path while reducing repeated queries.
experiments.notes: The one registered game completed normally. All 13,611 valid searches and two invalid-endpoint probes matched reachability, distance bits and ordered tiles; combined callback evaluations fell 91.02%. There was no state-hash mismatch.
experiments.conclusion: The observed equivalence check passed. Build a separate production candidate and measure it against the unchanged throughput gate; this diagnostic ran both algorithms and does not measure production speed.

experiments.title: McRave pathfinding memoization throughput check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen per-search A* memoization candidate completes ten fixed games cleanly with at least 384 durable logical frames per wall second in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Ten clean wins, with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and 20 hash-checked, parsed replays. Aggregate throughput reached 413.1 fps, but games 6–9 fell below 384; the slowest ran at 269.5 fps.
experiments.conclusion: The registered per-game performance gate failed. Preserve this candidate and profile the slowest scenario later in the game before choosing another optimization. These reused scenarios do not establish a causal speedup or strength improvement.

experiments.title: Profile McRave late in the game
experiments.hypothesis: A complete ten-second sample after frame 15,000 identifies a cohesive subsystem occupying at least 20% of main-thread observations.
experiments.notes: The match completed normally. The sample retained 7,165 stacks: Combat 23.8%, grid updates 18.9%, Support 11.8%. Its timestamp precedes game completion by only 9.110 seconds, so the required ten seconds of live sampling could not be established.
experiments.conclusion: Keep these counts as partial diagnostic evidence. Investigate repeated ground-path and Support path generation with a separately registered diagnostic; this sample does not pass its original gate.

experiments.title: Calibrate a local league on two new maps
experiments.hypothesis: Five exact build/race configurations complete twelve clean comparisons and form a connected graph on two previously unused maps.
experiments.notes: All twelve attempted; nine clean and three conflicting-winner outcomes. All 24 replays parse and match owner frames. Local estimates retain broad model-dependent intervals and prior sensitivity.
experiments.conclusion: The clean-cohort gate failed. Show the nine reviewed games as a partial uncalibrated league; investigate McRave–Stardust terminal integrity and McRave losses on Heartbreak Ridge. No promotion or BASIL estimate.

experiments.title: Local calibration: Stardust comparisons
experiments.notes: Part of the preregistered twelve-game local-calibration-v1 cohort. See the parent evaluation for the decision and uncertainty.
experiments.conclusion: Included only after per-game review; failures remain unscored. This sub-batch alone does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Local calibration: UAlberta comparisons
experiments.notes: Part of the preregistered twelve-game local-calibration-v1 cohort. See the parent evaluation for the decision and uncertainty.
experiments.conclusion: Included only after per-game review; failures remain unscored. This sub-batch alone does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Local calibration: McRave comparisons
experiments.notes: Part of the preregistered twelve-game local-calibration-v1 cohort. See the parent evaluation for the decision and uncertainty.
experiments.conclusion: Included only after per-game review; failures remain unscored. This sub-batch alone does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: First native game for Kestrel, our original bot
experiments.hypothesis: Kestrel completes a real headless match and demonstrates economy, production, scouting and combat.
experiments.notes: Both processes exited cleanly and both replays parsed. Kestrel lost to WorkerRush; repeated building commands and no trained combat unit failed the lifecycle gate.
experiments.conclusion: Keep the first replay and fix pending construction management before further strength evaluation. A diagnostic-fixture loss is not a calibrated rating.

experiments.title: Kestrel completes its production and combat lifecycle
experiments.hypothesis: Preserving the pending builder allows the original lifecycle to complete with at most 12 pylon/gateway build commands.
experiments.notes: Kestrel won its WorkerRush diagnostic smoke. Replay and telemetry show 27 probes, 5 pylons, 4 gateways, 9 zealots and 2 dragoons at peak; both replays parse and terminal results agree.
experiments.conclusion: The lifecycle passed, but 16 build commands exceed the registered 12-command ceiling. Retain as the first working lifecycle reference; continue command management. This fixture is not a rating anchor.

experiments.title: Kestrel faces ZZZK and UAlberta
experiments.hypothesis: The original bot completes two benchmark games with plausible production, fewer rejected commands and at least 384 durable fps.
experiments.notes: Both games completed with opposing outcomes and parsed replays; Kestrel lost both. ZZZK: 2557 fps and 18% of commands rejected. UAlberta: 3287 fps and 71% rejected; 16 pylon/gateway orders.
experiments.conclusion: Compatibility and lifecycle passed, but the command-quality gate failed. Fix repeated attack requests before expanding the strength cohort. Two losses do not provide a calibrated Elo.

experiments.title: Measure repeated McRave path searches
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded real-game diagnostic identifies a directly observed regeneration case representing at least 20% and 100 generated paths for a semantics-preserving shadow comparison.
experiments.notes: Support generated 24,676 JPS results; 23,795 were unreachable. Combat march generated 36,180 and retreat 33,569. Match ended cleanly with two retained replays.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the next diagnostic step only: test fresh per-search JPS callback memoization and count cheap rejection separately. No caching across frames, speed claim or bot promotion.

experiments.title: Repair conflicting results after natural defeat
experiments.hypothesis: Retaining a defeated peer until explicit leave or ordinary transport cleanup avoids early-EOF reciprocal winners.
experiments.notes: Six of six preregistered games completed cleanly. All four targets exercised the repair; both controls passed. Twelve replays parsed, with matching common action streams and no state-hash mismatch.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the frozen engine for new development experiments. Preserve older engine regimes and leave previous invalid games unscored.

experiments.title: Kestrel command cooldown probe
experiments.hypothesis: Per-unit request state and cooldowns reduce rejected combat requests while retaining production and legal combat.
experiments.notes: Both benchmark games completed cleanly with two parsed replay copies each. Rejected-command fractions were 43.5% against ZZZK and 42.4% against UAlberta Terran.
experiments.conclusion: Both command-quality gates failed. Target changes can bypass per-target cooldowns; test stable target retention with attributed command telemetry. No strength promotion.

experiments.title: Kestrel retains legal combat targets
experiments.hypothesis: Stable public target retention lowers rejected requests without suppressing production or combat.
experiments.notes: Both real-opponent games completed and were losses. Attack requests became mostly clean, but rejected training requests dominated: busy buildings and supply shortages.
experiments.conclusion: The overall command-quality gate failed. Preserve the targeting finding, then check public BWAPI training legality before issuing requests.

experiments.title: Check Support path-search memoization equivalence
experiments.hypothesis: A fresh per-search callback memo preserves reachability, exact distance and ordered path results in real Support searches.
experiments.notes: 16,773 comparisons produced zero mismatches. Callback evaluations fell 65.65%; most unreachable cases really searched rather than returning cheaply.
experiments.conclusion: Proceed to the separate production gate only. Diagnostic timing does not establish full-match speed or playing strength.

experiments.title: McRave Support memo: full-match performance gate
experiments.notes: Nine clean wins, one unscored old-engine terminal conflict. All 20 replay copies parse. Four valid games missed 384 fps; clean aggregate 366.7 fps.
experiments.conclusion: Reject engineering acceptance. The invalid result separately leaves integrity evidence incomplete; it cannot erase the valid slow-tail failures. Retain the isolated candidate for diagnosis, with no strength promotion.

experiments.title: Four-map local league on the repaired engine
experiments.hypothesis: The same five frozen build/race nodes form a clean connected comparison graph across four maps on the repaired engine.
experiments.notes: 24 of 24 registered games clean; 48 SHA-matching replay copies parsed with race/frame checks. Five exact build/race nodes connect across four maps. Current and historical engines remain separate.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the complete local rating display cohort, with wide conditional intervals and prior sensitivity. No bot promotion or BASIL-scale claim. Next compare Stardust directly with ZZZK and McRave with both UAlberta races.

experiments.title: Current-engine calibration: stardust
experiments.notes: Part of the 24-game four-map local-calibration-v2 cohort. All eight games in this sub-batch passed review.
experiments.conclusion: See the parent cohort for the complete graph and uncertainty; this sub-batch does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Current-engine calibration: uab-t
experiments.notes: Part of the 24-game four-map local-calibration-v2 cohort. All eight games in this sub-batch passed review.
experiments.conclusion: See the parent cohort for the complete graph and uncertainty; this sub-batch does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Current-engine calibration: mcrave
experiments.notes: Part of the 24-game four-map local-calibration-v2 cohort. All eight games in this sub-batch passed review.
experiments.conclusion: See the parent cohort for the complete graph and uncertainty; this sub-batch does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Kestrel passes training and combat command checks
experiments.hypothesis: Public BWAPI training checks remove avoidable busy/supply requests while preserving production and combat.
experiments.notes: Two clean benchmark losses with parsed replays. Zero train/attack rejections in both; overall rejection 0% against ZZZK and 4% against UAlberta Terran.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt as the first command-quality baseline. It remains strategically weak; next prioritize the first combat unit against early Zerg pressure. No win-rate or Elo promotion.

experiments.title: Explain McRave’s delayed Zerg opening
experiments.hypothesis: Crossing fixed seeds with two maps distinguishes opener selection from map-dependent production delay.
experiments.notes: All four games clean with paired replays. Seed 1001 chose 9Pool and seed 6301 chose Gaspool on both maps. Opener choice shifted first Zergling timing about 559 frames; within-opener map differences were 51–62 frames.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the diagnosis: selected opening explains the observed delay in these cells. Preregister a separate strategy comparison; this diagnostic does not establish a stronger bot.

experiments.title: Fill missing direct rating matchups
experiments.hypothesis: Direct Stardust–ZZZK and McRave–UAlberta comparisons add missing edges to the current exact-build graph.
experiments.notes: All 12 games clean with 24 hash-checked, parsed replay copies. Stardust–ZZZK 4–0; McRave–UAlberta Protoss 4–0 and Terran 3–1.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the complete extension for local display. Current-engine evidence now totals 36 games in one component. Intervals remain conditional and wide; no bot promotion or BASIL transfer.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests an earlier first Zealot
experiments.hypothesis: Prioritizing the first Zealot improves early exposure against Zerg pressure.
experiments.notes: The exact-row first Zealot train arrived 396 frames earlier, but Kestrel lost 16 workers and ended 62 frames sooner. The held-out game also failed lifecycle floors. Both games completed cleanly.
experiments.conclusion: Reject the strategy candidate and retain v7. Earlier training alone did not bridge the period before an army could defend workers. Test visible-threat worker defense separately.

experiments.title: Missing-edge calibration: stardust
experiments.notes: Reviewed sub-batch of the 12-game local-calibration-v3 extension.
experiments.conclusion: See the parent cohort for direct matchups and cumulative uncertainty. No bot promotion.

experiments.title: Missing-edge calibration: mcrave
experiments.notes: Reviewed sub-batch of the 12-game local-calibration-v3 extension.
experiments.conclusion: See the parent cohort for direct matchups and cumulative uncertainty. No bot promotion.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests worker defense near home
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded worker pull against visible ground threats improves early defense while preserving production.
experiments.notes: Both games completed cleanly. Six previously harvesting probes engaged near-home threats and later returned to gathering, but Kestrel lost 18 and 16 workers and produced only one and two Zealots.
experiments.conclusion: Reject the worker-pull candidate. Matched survival and army-production gates failed; v7 remains the accepted command-quality baseline. Scout contact timestamps are distinct from threats reaching home.

experiments.title: McRave tests a fixed 9Pool opening
experiments.hypothesis: Changing only the selected ZvZ PoolLair opener to 9Pool improves matched outcomes against ZZZK while meeting resource guards.
experiments.notes: All 16 games valid and all 32 replay copies hash-checked and parsed. Treatment won 7/8 versus control 6/8. Two of four effective pairs improved, with no effective regression; an unchanged-opening pair flipped against treatment.
experiments.conclusion: Advance only to independent confirmation. Minimum treatment throughput 631.9 fps and CPU/frame +0.43% passed the guards. The one-win overall advantage and no-op outcome variation do not justify production adoption.

experiments.title: Kestrel delays gas for early Zealots
experiments.hypothesis: Delaying Zerg-matchup gas and Core spending produces a defensive army sooner without changing micro.
experiments.notes: Both games completed cleanly with zero rejected commands. Gas was delayed, but the matched third Zealot train was only 132 frames earlier than v7, below the required 200; neither game queued a fourth Zealot.
experiments.conclusion: Reject the timing and lifecycle result. Keep v7 and inspect the first home engagement with public-state telemetry before another policy change.

experiments.title: Kestrel traces its first home fight
experiments.hypothesis: Public-state traces can distinguish delayed production, misplaced combat units and ineffective engagement in the fixed v7 loss.
experiments.notes: One instrumented v7 game, Benzene seed 6103, with no policy change. Both clients exited cleanly and both replays parsed. This is diagnostic evidence, not a rating or performance trial.
experiments.conclusion: The first two Zealots fought near home but arrived separately against five and then at least eight Zerglings. The second Gateway started too late to contribute to the first fight, while minerals were banked. Test earlier second-Gateway construction; this single trace does not establish a general cause or a strength improvement.

experiments.title: Kestrel moves its second Gateway before gas
experiments.hypothesis: Earlier second-Gateway construction against known Zerg will provide two completed Zealots together near home before the first defender dies.
experiments.notes: Two fixed games against ZZZK, Benzene seed 6103 and Heartbreak seed 6104. Both completed cleanly with zero rejected commands and parsed replay pairs. Native and official BWAPI header compilation passed.
experiments.conclusion: Both games lost with at most one completed Zealot in the home-fight window. The second Gateway appeared by frame 2904/2894 but completed at 3875/3865, after home pressure at 3704/3590. Earlier capacity alone did not satisfy the mechanism or lifecycle checks; retain v7.

experiments.title: Check UAlberta Zerg as a second opponent
experiments.hypothesis: Frozen UAlbertaBot can complete its configured Zerg production and full games against the McRave candidate at the required 384 frames per second.
experiments.notes: Two fixed games completed cleanly with four fully parsed and hashed replays. UAlberta produced Drones, a Spawning Pool and Zerglings in both. Zero terminal unit counters describe survivors after defeat, not cumulative production.
experiments.conclusion: Gameplay compatibility passed, but Destination ran at 314.6 fps, below the fixed 384-fps requirement; Benzene ran at 418.8 fps. The McRave-side process is the first profiling target. No retry or strength promotion.

experiments.title: Kestrel reserves minerals for its first Pylon
experiments.hypothesis: Protecting the pending first Pylon’s mineral cost will let a single accepted build order start construction within 120 frames while preserving normal production.
experiments.notes: Both fixed games issued only one first-Pylon build order. Benzene took 289 frames to start construction; Heartbreak took 115. Both games completed with parsed replay pairs. The once-only guard was corrected before either trial.
experiments.conclusion: The registered screen failed: Benzene exceeded the 120-frame limit, and Heartbreak rejected 11 of 68 commands, all build Unit_Busy errors. Both games lost. Keep v7; distinguish builder travel and command conflicts before another opening change.

experiments.title: McRave profiling launch failed before initialization
experiments.hypothesis: A complete ten-second sample after frame 15000 will identify a McRave subsystem accounting for at least 20% of main-thread samples.
experiments.notes: The single allowed launch used the default sandbox and failed local socket setup before gameplay. Both clients printed connect errors; no telemetry, samples or replay was produced. The failed attempt remains preserved.
experiments.conclusion: No profiling evidence. This evaluation is closed without a retry. A separately registered v2 corrects the execution environment while retaining the same measurement and decision rules.

experiments.title: Profile McRave’s slower Zerg matchup
experiments.hypothesis: A complete ten-second sample after frame 15000 will identify a McRave subsystem accounting for at least 20% of main-thread samples.
experiments.notes: One diagnostic game with a verified live ten-second sample and 8,032 main-thread observations. The archived trigger snapshot is frame 18,720. The game completed cleanly; its instrumented outcome and runtime are excluded from strength and throughput comparisons.
experiments.conclusion: Grid updates accounted for 1,611 samples (20.06%), meeting the diagnostic threshold. Repeated walk-position validity checks accounted for 641 samples (7.98%). Compare cached public map bounds with the existing predicate on identical inputs before any production change.

experiments.title: Kestrel traces rejected building commands
experiments.hypothesis: Worker-level traces will distinguish command ownership conflicts from travel delays in rejected construction requests.
experiments.notes: One fixed Heartbreak game produced 265 trace records, nine build attempts and two rejected attempts. Both replays were preserved and the game completed cleanly.
experiments.conclusion: Both rejected requests reused a Probe while it was harvesting gas; no gather command had been issued in either cadence. The same Probe could build after leaving the refinery. Test excluding gas workers from construction selection, including cached-builder reuse.

experiments.title: Check cached map bounds against the existing predicate
experiments.hypothesis: Cached public map dimensions will produce exactly the same walk-position validity result as the current API call.
experiments.notes: One full Destination game compared 1,757,500,992 real inputs and eight negative, boundary and invalid-sentinel cases. Existing API results remained authoritative for gameplay. Native and 114 official-header translation units compiled.
experiments.conclusion: Zero disagreements; the game completed cleanly with both replays retained. The result supports a narrowly scoped replacement and a separate performance test. Frequent diagnostic writes prevent timing or strength claims from this run.

experiments.title: Kestrel avoids gas workers when choosing builders
experiments.hypothesis: Excluding gas-gathering Probes from construction selection will remove the reproduced build Unit_Busy failure while preserving economy and army production.
experiments.notes: Both registered games exercised the guard: one event against ZZZK and seven against UAlberta Terran. Gas-worker build attempts and build Unit_Busy errors were zero. Total rejected commands stayed below 5%; all four replay copies parsed and throughput exceeded 384 fps.
experiments.conclusion: Adopted as Kestrel’s development baseline after source and evidence review. Both games were losses, so this is a narrow construction-reliability improvement and does not establish stronger play.

experiments.title: McRave cached-bounds performance screen
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing repeated walk-position API checks with equivalent cached map bounds will reduce process CPU per frame by at least 5% without paired regressions.
experiments.notes: Eight matched attempts completed cleanly; all 16 replay copies passed full parsing and hash checks. Aggregate candidate CPU per frame was 107.43% of control, and two pairs exceeded the 110% regression guard. Memory and outcome guards passed.
experiments.conclusion: Rejected: the candidate did not improve measured performance and will not advance. Two candidate games also fell below 384 durable frames per second. All outcomes and artifacts are retained; the baseline is unchanged.

experiments.title: Kestrel reserves minerals for its first Gateway and Zealot
experiments.hypothesis: A one-time opening mineral reserve will advance the first Gateway request and first Zealot training by at least 120 frames in both matched scenarios.
experiments.notes: Four fresh control/candidate games passed the registered screen. Gateway requests advanced by 348 and 186 frames; Zealot training advanced by 432 and 228 frames. Candidate commands had zero rejection; all eight replays parsed.
experiments.conclusion: The opening mechanism passed and may advance to broader confirmation. Both candidate games still lost; canonical Kestrel v13 is unchanged and no playing-strength gain is established.

experiments.title: Strengthen the local rating comparisons
experiments.hypothesis: Direct games on a missing reference edge and a close matchup will improve the evidence supporting the existing local rating model.
experiments.notes: Twelve registered games completed cleanly and all 24 replays passed full parsing and hash checks. UAlberta Protoss went 5–1 against Terran and 1–5 against ZZZK. Exact node and engine identities match the previous cohorts.
experiments.conclusion: Accepted for rating display after independent manifest and replay-hash review. The unchanged model now uses 48 current-engine games. Conditional intervals narrowed, but remain wide; this is uncalibrated local evidence and does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: Inspect Kestrel’s earlier first defenders
experiments.hypothesis: Public fight traces can distinguish distant chasing or target switching from losing sequential fights near home.
experiments.notes: One instrumented v14 game completed cleanly with both replays parsed. The first completed Zealot faced six visible Zerglings near home; the second arrived after the first had died and faced at least seven.
experiments.conclusion: The trace supports a lack of overlapping defenders. It did not show distant chasing or harmful target switching. Test earlier second-Gateway production from the faster v14 opening; this single diagnostic does not establish a general cause or strength change.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests overlapping two-Gateway defense
experiments.hypothesis: Adding earlier second-Gateway production to v14 and delaying gas until four Zealot trains will produce two completed local defenders before the first local loss.
experiments.notes: Both candidate games built two Gateways and accepted four Zealot trains, but reached only one completed local defender before the first loss. Heartbreak also missed the registered later-construction guard. All four games were clean and all eight replays parsed.
experiments.conclusion: Rejected. Earlier second-Gateway construction still did not create overlapping defenders in time. Both candidates lost; canonical Kestrel v13 is unchanged.

experiments.title: Check cached map bounds for McRave visibility updates
experiments.hypothesis: Restricting visibility iteration to the loaded map rectangle will reduce McRave CPU per frame without changing visibility results.
experiments.notes: Phase 1 passed with 2,314,338,304 gameplay comparisons, zero mismatches and all eight boundary sentinels. The diagnostic-free candidate compiled natively and against 114 official BWAPI headers. Phase 2 stopped on its first attempt because the local socket was unavailable before game start; no retry or replacement was made.
experiments.conclusion: Inconclusive: the correctness shadow passed, but the registered performance cohort had no valid game. The candidate was not advanced or adopted, and the prior direct-bounds rejection remains unchanged.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests first-Pylon reservation
experiments.hypothesis: Reserving 100 minerals for the first Pylon after six completed Probes will move the V15 production sequence early enough for two completed local Zealots to overlap before the first local loss.
experiments.notes: The candidate accepted its first Pylon 192 to 264 frames earlier and its first Gateway 291 to 326 frames earlier than matched controls, but reached only one local completed Zealot before the first loss in both games. Heartbreak also recorded three accepted Zealot trains and no accepted structure after the first train. All four games were clean and all eight replays parsed.
experiments.conclusion: Rejected. Earlier first-Pylon timing did not produce overlapping defenders and was worse than the matched controls on the registered local-overlap gate. Canonical Kestrel v13 remains unchanged; v16 does not advance to held-out comparison.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests a wider supply buffer
experiments.hypothesis: Requesting the next supply Pylon at a six-supply margin will preserve the faster v16 opening while allowing two local Zealots to overlap before the first local loss.
experiments.notes: The candidate still built only one Pylon in both games and accepted no structure after its first Zealot. It reached one local completed Zealot before first loss on both maps; Heartbreak also reached only nine Probes. All four games were clean and all eight replays parsed.
experiments.conclusion: Rejected. The wider supply margin did not reach a second-Pylon request before pressure and did not improve the registered overlap or production gates. Canonical Kestrel v13 remains unchanged.

experiments.title: Kestrel tests explicit second-Pylon priority
experiments.hypothesis: Requesting a second Pylon before the second-Gateway branch will repair v16/v17's missing supply structure and produce two local defenders before the first loss.
experiments.notes: The candidate reached two Pylons in both games, but the second Gateway completed 271 to 293 frames later than matched controls. It accepted three Zealot trains and reached only one local defender before first loss on both maps; Heartbreak also reached nine Probes and no post-first-train structure. All four games were clean and all eight replays parsed.
experiments.conclusion: Rejected. The explicit supply repair delayed army production and did not meet the overlap gate. Canonical Kestrel v13 remains unchanged.
